subject: Colonization and extinction having the same behaviour - colext

messages.author: 014d00e7482d028b
messages.subject: Colonization and extinction having the same behaviour - colext
parts:
Dear all,

Not really a methodological question, but rather an interpretation.
I modelled a couple of species roadkill through a dynamic occupancy model (using colext function) through a period of >10 years in the same sampled roads (divided into ~500 segments). 
When retrieving mean values for colonization and extinction and plotting the results for each year (to explore the temporal component) I have an example where both the colonization and extinction present high values for the same year. The values are rather low (colonization ~ 0.4 and extinction ~0.2), but they are high when compared with other years. Does it make any sense that a species can present both colonization and extinction in the same year? I remember it is a mean value for each year including all ~500 sites. 
I don't know if I have made myself clear.

Any assistance would be greatly appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: Colonization and extinction having the same behaviour - colext
parts: If you have high colonization and high extinction, you effectively have high turnover. High turnover indicates the sites where species are located changed a lot in that year, i.e., they left the sites where they were in the previous year and colonized new sites, even if the total number of sites remained the same.

messages.author: bed9858844040a0b
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Re: Colonization and extinction having the same behaviour - colext
parts:
Colonization is the probability (or rate) of previously unoccupied sites becoming occupied, whereas extinction is the probability (or rate) of previously occupied sites becoming unoccupied. So, no neither is averaging across all sites. Mean colonization is averaged across previously unoccupied sites and mean extinction is averaged across previously occupied sites. If in the initial year occupancy is 0.5 and you have 100 sites in your sample, colonization will be the rate at which the 50 sites that were not occupied became occupied, and extinction is the rate at which the other 50 sites that were occupied became unoccupied.

 

Quresh S. Latif 
Research Scientist
Bird Conservancy of the Rockies

www.birdconservancy.org
